heroHeadline: Day 92 of Op Ghazab — Jawid Niazi Day 22 in Taliban GDI Custody; UN Experts Reiterate Alarm Over Decree No. 18 Child Marriage; 23-Day Strike Pause; WFP Needs $313M Urgently
heroSubtitle: On May 28, 2026 (Day 92 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), Paigard News Agency director Jawid (Ahmad Jawed) Niazi remained in Taliban General Directorate of Intelligence (GDI) custody for a 22nd consecutive day — the longest of the three journalist detentions since May 6. TOLO News journalists Mansoor Niazi and Imran Danish, released on bail on May 27, face pending trials after Eid al-Adha; both remain in Afghanistan. Afghanistan International reported on May 27-28 that UN human rights experts continued to press the Taliban to revoke Decree No. 18, which treats a 'virgin girl's' silence as implicit consent to marriage — effectively enabling child marriage under Taliban family law. The 23-day pause in confirmed Pakistani cross-border airstrikes since the May 5 Dangam (Kunar) strike holds. WFP urgently needs $313 million to address the malnutrition crisis affecting 4.9 million Afghan mothers and children, as 500,000+ deportees from Pakistan and Iran in 2026 worsen conditions — the 2026 UN appeal is 60% unfunded. Russia's May 26 declaration of 'full-fledged partnership' with the Taliban at SCO Moscow (where Yaqoob Mujahid attended) continues to complicate Pakistan's leverage in future ceasefire negotiations. No formal ceasefire; no Urumqi Round 2 date; China silent on mediation since April 8.
